newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PNG-Australia gas line unaffected by politics.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PNG-Australia gas line unaffected by politics.

text.p: Political instability in Papua New Guinea (PNG) would not stand in the way of Chevron Corp's planned A$2 billion Australia-PNG gas pipeline project, Rich Farley, Chevron's commercial pipeline manager said.
"We've been producing oil (in PNG) for more than five years with several transitions of government (and) we haven't had a day of lost production," he told Reuters.

PNG Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan on Monday sacked army commander Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok after he called on Chan to quit over his plan to use mercenaries to end the secessionist conflict on Bougainville.
Farley said the group had good relations with the government and local landowners.
"Everyone's pleased with our project and no matter what happens in the political arena there it will go forward," he said.
Chevron Corp is seeking participants for construction, ownership and operation of the project, to consist of gas production and LPG extraction and processing facilities.

The pipeline was planned to run from PNG to the Australian border, then in successive stages Townsville and to Gladstone, both in the Australian state of Queensland, for commercial delivery in north Queensland and potentially central Queensland by about July 2000.
It would draw gas from the Kutubu and other gas fields in PNG. The Pandora gas field offshore in the Gulf of Papua could also be tied in to the pipeline as markets expanded, Chevron has said.

The Pandora joint-venture is headed by Canada's International Petroleum Corp (48.1890 percent), Mobil Corp unit Ampolex Ltd (16.3636 percent), the Command Petroleum Ltd subsidiary of Cairn Energy Plc (12.7273 percent), Beach Petroleum NL (6.3636) and Oil Search Ltd and Secab Mining Pty Ltd (5.0 percent each).

Kutubu participants are Chevron Niugini Pty Ltd (19.375 percent), Oil Search (7.763 percent), Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd unit BHP Petroleum (PNG) Inc (9.688 percent), BP Australia Ltd 19.375 percent), Ampolex 16.455 (percent), Mitsubishi Oil co Ltd affiliate JPP (4.844 percent) and the PNG government (22.50 percent).
Oil Search's managing director Peter Botten has said that development of the new fields of Gobe and Moran, nearby Kutubu, were unlikely to be disrupted by political unrest.

Gobe was expected to begin production early next year at an initial 50,000 barrels of crude a day, while Oil Search has said its promising Moran field was expected to have greater reserves than Kutubu's proven and probable reserves of 280 million barrels of oil.
